text:
arjun: FYI seeing ArgoCD sync jitter in eu-west this morning. Multiple app-of-apps syncs overlap prune waves and we get 429s hitting api-server during GPU pool scaleups.

maria: yep saw that. Two clusters performing simultaneous autoscale from spot -> on-demand -> capacity wait. Syncs keep retrying and queueing.

sam: any errors in controller logs? can you paste snippet?

arjun: paste: ```time="2026-03-18T09:11:12Z" level=error msg="rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc=apiserver rate limited" app=infra-gpu-pool```

evan: we also had helm pre-sync hooks creating jobs that stuck; that keeps finalizers blocking prune.

arjun: runbook link: https://redwoodinternal/runbooks/gitops-prune-windowing — suggests staggered prune windows. but our app-of-apps fanout config is wide.

maria: suggestion: add jitter to appset schedule and limit parallelism in app-of-apps (reduce fanout via labels/selectors), also increase argocd server burst. But we're hitting cost constraints if we up control-plane size.

sam: can we throttle prune waves with argocd.app-of-apps annotation? we currently set `argocd.argoproj.io/sync-options: Prune=true`.

evan: quick mitigation: disable concurrentSyncs in argocd-cm and add `--repo-server-burst`? we tried raising kube-apiserver burst already but not enough.

maria: also found terraform drift: the appset replicas for eu-* were accidentally set to 50 -> should be 5. PR coming.

arjun: opening a short maintenance window and will roll out staggered appset batches. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/terraform/merge/1234

infra-bot: deploy started: terraform apply plan-1234 by arjun — 10:02 UTC :gear:

sam: OK will watch ArgoCD metrics and apiserver latency. If 429s persist we'll fallback to read-only prune schedule.

maria: noted — cost impact if we increase control-plane. prefer config change and stagger first.

arjun: thanks. I'll post follow-ups in ~30m with metrics. :thumbsup:
